before.title: Finite speed of propagation for linear symmetric hyperbolic systems: cone domination and independence of the extension
before.statement:
Let $T>0$, let $A^\mu:(-T,T)\times\mathbb R^3\to\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$
($\mu=0,1,2,3$) be smooth with $A^0(t,x)\ge aI$ for some constant $a>0$ and all
$(t,x)$, and let $\|A^i(t,x)\|\le b$ for the operator norm and all $i,t,x$. Let
$C:(-T,T)\times\mathbb R^3\to M_m(\mathbb R)$ be smooth and bounded by $K$.

**(a)** Put $\lambda:=b/a+1$; then $\lambda A^0(t,x)+\xi_iA^i(t,x)\ge0$ as a
quadratic form for every $(t,x)$ and every $\xi\in\mathbb R^3$ with
$|\xi|\le1$.

**(b)** Let $w\in C^1((-T,T)\times\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^m)$ solve
$$A^0\partial_tw+A^i\partial_iw+Cw=0 ,$$
and let $x_0\in\mathbb R^3$, $0<t_0<T$, and suppose $w(0,x)=0$ for every
$|x-x_0|\le\lambda t_0$. Then $w(t,x)=0$ for every
$(t,x)\in\{(t,x):0\le t\le t_0,\ |x-x_0|\le\lambda(t_0-t)\}$.

**(c)** [independence of the extension] If $w_1,w_2$ are two solutions of two
such systems whose coefficient matrices agree on an open set containing the
truncated cone $D=\{(t,x):0\le t\le t_0,|x-x_0|\le\lambda(t_0-t)\}$, and if
$w_1(0,x)=w_2(0,x)$ for $|x-x_0|\le\lambda t_0$, then $w_1=w_2$ on $D$.

references.title: H. Friedrich and A. D. Rendall, The Cauchy Problem for the Einstein Equations, Living Reviews in Relativity 3 (2000), article 1 (arXiv:gr-qc/0002074), Section 3.1 (Symmetric Hyperbolic Systems): the definition of a quasilinear symmetric hyperbolic system, the finite-dimensional mollifier approximation (3.1) solved by ODE theory, the energy and Moser product/composition estimates, the higher-order energy inequality, uniqueness, the Rellich/Ascoli compactness step and the passage to a classical solution, with Remarks 1-6 on smooth persistence, the continuation criterion, Cauchy stability and the non-identity time matrix

H. Friedrich and A. D. Rendall, The Cauchy Problem for the Einstein Equations, Living Reviews in Relativity 3 (2000), article 1 (arXiv:gr-qc/0002074), Section 3.2 (Symmetric Hyperbolic Systems on Manifolds): the invariant principal-symbol definition of a symmetric hyperbolic system on a manifold, with Section 3.1's torus theory supplying the local model

**(a)** Put $\lambda:=\sqrt3\,b/a+1$; then $\lambda A^0(t,x)+\xi_iA^i(t,x)\ge0$ as a
quadratic form for every $(t,x)$ and every $\xi\in\mathbb R^3$ with
$|\xi|\le1$.

**(c)** [independence of the extension] If $w_1,w_2$ are two solutions of two
such systems whose complete coefficient families, including $C$, agree on an open set containing the
truncated cone $D=\{(t,x):0\le t\le t_0,|x-x_0|\le\lambda(t_0-t)\}$, and if
$w_1(0,x)=w_2(0,x)$ for $|x-x_0|\le\lambda t_0$, then $w_1=w_2$ on $D$.

citations.quote: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. If Omega has the specified finite piecewise $C^1$ presentation and $F\in C^1(\overline\Omega;\mathbb R^n)$, then $\int_\Omega\operatorname{div}F=\sum_j\int_{S_j}F\cdot\nu_j\,dS$, with faces counted once off E. All integrals are finite. In a specified finite gluing, the two fluxes on every shared face cancel.

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. For $F:[a,b]\to\mathbb R$, the following are equivalent:

1. $F$ is absolutely continuous.
2. $F'$ exists almost everywhere, $F'\in L^1[a,b]$, and
$$F(x)-F(a)=\int_a^xF'(t)\,dt\quad\text{for every }x\in[a,b].$$

Let $t_0\le T$, let $u,a,b:[t_0,T]\to\mathbb R$ be continuous, with $u,b\ge0$, and suppose

$$u(t)\le a(t)+\int_{t_0}^t b(s)u(s)\,ds.$$

Then

$$u(t)\le a(t)+\int_{t_0}^t a(s)b(s)\exp\!\left(\int_s^t b(r)\,dr\right)ds.$$

If $a$ is nondecreasing, this gives $u(t)\le a(t)\exp(\int_{t_0}^t b)$. The time-reflected form assumes $u(t)\le a(t)+\int_t^{t_0}b(s)u(s)\,ds$ for $t\le t_0$. In particular, when $a=A\ge0$ and $b=B\ge0$ are constant, the two orientations give $u(t)\le A e^{B|t-t_0|}$.

derivations.claim: (The cone condition (a).) By [L1], $\lambda:=b/a+1$ gives $z^{\mathsf T}(\lambda A^0+\xi_iA^i)z\ge((b/a+1)a-b)|z|^2=|z|^2>0$ for $z\ne0$ and $|\xi|\le1$; so the quadratic form is positive definite, in particular nonnegative. This is (a).

(The cone inequality.) Suppose $w$ solves the system and put $j^\mu:=w^{\mathsf T}A^\mu w$, a $C^1$ vector field. Then $\operatorname{div}_{(t,x)}j=\partial_t(w^{\mathsf T}A^0w)+\partial_i(w^{\mathsf T}A^iw)=2w^{\mathsf T}(A^0\partial_tw+A^i\partial_iw)+w^{\mathsf T}(\partial_tA^0+\partial_iA^i)w=-2w^{\mathsf T}Cw+w^{\mathsf T}(\partial_tA^0+\partial_iA^i)w\le K'w^{\mathsf T}w\le(K'/a)j^0$, where $K':=2K+\sup|\partial_tA^0+\partial_iA^i|$.

(Flux through the truncated cone.) For $0<\tau<t_0$ let $D_\tau:=\{(s,x):0\le s\le\tau,\ |x-x_0|\le\lambda(t_0-s)\}$, so that $\partial D_\tau$ consists of the base $B_0:=\{(0,x):|x-x_0|\le\lambda t_0\}$, the lateral surface $L_\tau:=\{ |x-x_0|=\lambda(t_0-s),\ 0\le s\le\tau\}$, and the top $B_\tau:=\{\tau\}\times\{|x-x_0|\le\lambda(t_0-\tau)\}$. On the base the outward normal is $-\partial_t$, so the flux is $-\int_{B_0}j^0$; on the top it is $+\int_{B_\tau}j^0$; on the lateral surface the outward unit normal is $\nu=(\lambda,\xi)/\sqrt{1+\lambda^2}$ with $\xi=(x-x_0)/|x-x_0|$ and $|\xi|=1$, so the flux is $(1+\lambda^2)^{-1/2}\int_{L_\tau}w^{\mathsf T}(\lambda A^0+\xi_iA^i)w\,dS\ge0$ by (a). Integrating the inequality of step 1.2 over $D_\tau$ and using the divergence theorem [L2] gives $E(\tau):=\int_{B_\tau}j^0\le\int_{B_0}j^0+(K'/a)\int_0^\tau E(s)\,ds-\int_{L_\tau}(\cdots)\le\int_{B_0}j^0+(K'/a)\int_0^\tau E(s)\,ds$, since the lateral flux is nonnegative.

(Conclusion (b).) If the data vanish on $B_0$, then $E(\tau)\le(K'/a)\int_0^\tau E(s)\,ds$; since $E\ge0$ is continuous (even absolutely continuous) in $\tau$, Gronwall [L3] gives $E=0$ on $[0,t_0)$, hence $w=0$ on $\bigcup_{\tau<t_0}\overline{D_\tau}=D$ by continuity. This is (b).

(Independence (c).) If two systems agree on a neighborhood of $D$ and their solutions agree on $B_0$, then $w:=w_1-w_2$ solves a linear system of the same form with the common leading coefficients $A^\mu$ and with $C$ the coefficient of the difference (a bounded smooth matrix built from the two zeroth-order coefficients, using that the equations coincide on the neighborhood), and $w=0$ on $B_0$; step 3.1 applies and gives $w=0$ on $D$. This is (c).

after.claim: (Correct symbol domination.) For every $|\xi|\le1$, $\|\sum_i\xi_iA^i\|\le\sum_i|\xi_i|\|A^i\|\le b\|\xi\|_1\le\sqrt3\,b$. Hence for every $z$ one has $z^{\mathsf T}(\lambda A^0+\xi_iA^i)z\ge(\lambda a-\sqrt3b)|z|^2=a|z|^2\ge0$. This proves (a).

(Energy-current inequality on the compact cone.) Put $j^\mu=w^{\mathsf T}A^\mu w$. Symmetry and the equation give $\partial_\mu j^\mu=w^{\mathsf T}(\partial_tA^0+\sum_i\partial_iA^i-C-C^{\mathsf T})w$. On compact D let $M=\sup_D\|\partial_tA^0+\sum_i\partial_iA^i\|+2K<\infty$. Thus $\partial_\mu j^\mu\le M|w|^2\le(M/a)j^0$ throughout D.

(Truncated cone flux.) For $0<\tau<t_0$, apply the divergence theorem to $D_\tau=\{(s,x):0\le s\le\tau,|x-x_0|\le\lambda(t_0-s)\}$. Base flux is $-E(0)$ and top flux is $E(\tau)$, where $E(s)=\int_{|x-x_0|\le\lambda(t_0-s)}j^0(s,x)\,dx$. The lateral outward unit normal is $(\lambda,\xi)/\sqrt{1+\lambda^2}$, so its flux is nonnegative by step 1.1. Step 1.2 gives $E(\tau)\le E(0)+(M/a)\int_0^\tau E(s)\,ds$. The domains avoid the cone vertex, so their boundaries are piecewise C1 as required.

(Vanishing and the vertex.) $E$ is continuous and nonnegative; zero initial data give $E(0)=0$. Gronwall therefore gives $E(s)=0$ for $0\le s<t_0$. Positivity of $A^0$ and continuity of w imply w vanishes on each closed top ball, since a nonzero value would give positive integral on a neighborhood. Letting s increase to t_0 and using continuity also gives $w(t_0,x_0)=0$. This proves (b).

(Independence.) On the common neighborhood of D, subtract the two identical linear equations. The difference $w_1-w_2$ solves the homogeneous system with the common matrices $A^\mu$ and the common zeroth-order coefficient C; it vanishes on the base. The preceding argument uses only coefficients on D and gives equality throughout D. This proves (c).
